newsitem.title: BELGIUM: UCB sees no impact from UK drugs ruling.
newsitem.headline: UCB sees no impact from UK drugs ruling.

text.p: Belgian chemicals and drugs group UCB said on Monday it did not expect any positive impact on sales of its anti-allergy Zyrtec product after some rival drugs were withdrawn from over-the-counter (OTC) sale in the UK.
"It's too early to say (whether there will be a positive impact), but we don't expect any great changes. It's a very well known story," UCB spokesman Alain Douxchamps told Reuters.

Britain's Health Ministry said last month it intended to withdraw the hay fever remedy drug terfenadine from OTC sale at chemists because of fears some patients could suffer side effects. The drug could eventually become prescription only.
The decision affects a number of Zyrtec's rival OTC products.
Douxchamps said, however, medical evidence of side-effects linked to terfenadine and some other antihistamines had been known in the U.S. and continental Europe for years.
"I don't think it will change market trends for the time being, because it's a well-known story," Douxchamps said.
